preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is between 1 and 10^4.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 2 * 10**5 for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(t)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the length of the permutation n is between 1 and 2 * 10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= q_i <= n for q_i in map(int, input().split())) for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(t)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, each element q_i in the array q is between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(q == [max(q[:i+1]) for i in range(len(q))] for q in [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(t)])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the array q is obtained by applying the rule q_i = max(p_1, p_2, ..., p_i) to some permutation p.

preconditions.expression: sum(n for n in [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(t)]) <= 2 * 10**5
preconditions.description: The sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 2 * 10^5.

postconditions.expression: all(len(min_perm) == n and len(max_perm) == n for min_perm, max_perm, n in zip(min_perms, max_perms, [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, both the lexicographically minimal and maximal permutations have length n.

postconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= p_i <= n for p_i in min_perm) and all(1 <= p_i <= n for p_i in max_perm) for min_perm, max_perm, n in zip(min_perms, max_perms, [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, all elements in both the lexicographically minimal and maximal permutations are between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all(len(set(min_perm)) == n and len(set(max_perm)) == n for min_perm, max_perm, n in zip(min_perms, max_perms, [int(input().split()[0]) for _ in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, both the lexicographically minimal and maximal permutations are permutations of numbers from 1 to n.

postconditions.expression: all(all(min_perm[i] <= min_perm[j] for i in range(len(min_perm)) for j in range(i+1, len(min_perm))) for min_perm in min_perms)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the lexicographically minimal permutation is indeed the smallest possible permutation that could have produced q.

postconditions.expression: all(all(max_perm[i] >= max_perm[j] for i in range(len(max_perm)) for j in range(i+1, len(max_perm))) for max_perm in max_perms)
postconditions.description: For each test case, the lexicographically maximal permutation is indeed the largest possible permutation that could have produced q.
